summary: Alexander Duff (1806–1878) worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of St Andrews from circa 1821 to 1829 and at the University of Aberdeen, later teaching Krishna Mohan Banerjee.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy from circa 1900 to 1903 and under Christian Bartholomae from circa 1906 to 1907.

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan by 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also studied under Robert H. Sharf and Janet Gyatso, and held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander Hamilton (1762–1824) was an Indologist who taught figures including Friedrich Schlegel and Franz Bopp. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the East India Company College starting in 1806.
Alexander James O'Neill is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Japanology. A PhD candidate at the University of Toronto, he has served as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Christian Friedrich Schwarz, at the University of Göttingen (~1792–1795), and at Lincoln's Inn (~1795–1798), later serving on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819).

Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2003) worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek (1802–1870) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He held posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1849–1870).

Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) is a linguist and Indologist. Educated at Moscow State University and Leiden University, where he completed his PhD under Robert S. P. Beekes (~1978–1987), he became Professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).
Alexander Murray (1775–1813) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1794 to 1802 and held a post there from circa 1812 to 1813.

Alexander O. Hsu specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago Divinity School (~2011–2018) under supervisors Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

Alexander Piatigorsky (1929–2009) was an Indologist and philosopher. After studying at Moscow State University (~1946–1951), he worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and later served as Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia at SOAS (1990–2001).

Alexander Rogers (1825–1910) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at the East India Company College from circa 1843 to 1845 and subsequently served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel works in religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2008, he completed a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.
Alexander Studholme (born 1967) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin from circa 1996 to 2000.

Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He was affiliated with the CNRS (~1952–1975) and served as a professor at Paris Nanterre University from circa 1975 to 1991.

Alexander Wynne (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later serving as a Junior Research Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (2002–2006).

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Supervised by Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017), he also studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under teachers including Sherab Sangpo and Khenpo Sherab Dorje.

Alexander von Humboldt (1769–1859) worked in history and archaeology among other fields. He studied at European University Viadrina, Göttingen, Freiberg, and Jena, and later held a post at the University of Jena.
